newsitem.title: JORDAN: Mideast and African port conditions - Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: Mideast and African port conditions - Lloyds.

text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --
JORDAN, June 7 - Aqaba - Two vessels loading at berth, 9 discharging at berth, 2 waiting at anchorage to load, 1 waiting to discharge, 2 awaiting orders.

MOZAMBIQUE, June 9 - Nacala - Port working normally. No restrictions on berthing and sailing at night. Draft restrictions 9.5 metres at general cargo berth and 14 metres at container berth. One tug available. Beira - General cargo berths working normally. Container terminal/other terminals working normally. 24 Hour berthing/sailing for vessels up to 140 metres loa, some restrictions for larger vessels and subject to prior arrangements with port captain. Maximum draft for 24 hour navigation 7.5 metres. Two tugs available. General access channel two wave-rider buoys deployed in approach channel WMON1 19 deg. 66.0460 s 36 deg. 01.6698 e and WMON2 19 deg. 62.6370 s 34 deg. 62.6497 e. Approximate diameter 1 metre, flashing orange light, flash frequency of five one-second flashes every 36 seconds. Maputo - 24 Hour berthing/sailing for vessels up to 120 metres loa, some restrictions for larger vessels and subject to prior arrangement with port captain. All berths working normally, expected to remain so. Draft re
NAMIBIA, June 9 - Walvis Bay - Port working normally.

NIGERIA, June 10 - Lagos - Port operations slowed due to heavy rains. Rain and fuel shortages are disrupting transport. Fuel shortages becoming more severe in the Lagos area reportedly due to a reduction in imports and reduced refinery capacity. Port Harcourt - Port and city quiet. All other crude oil terminals working according to programme.

SOUTH AFRICA, June 9 - Richards Bay - General cargo berths working normally. Bulk import berths - Working normally. Bulk export berths (minerals etc.) - Working normally at present, but delays of 48 hrs. expected from 11-18/6. Bulk coal berths - 4 Vessels berthed, 2 due 9/6 and a further 22 due up to and including 16/6. Berthing delays of approx. 3-4 days are being experienced at present. Durban - Container terminal delays of up to 60 hours can be expected whilst 2 new noel cranes are being positioned. Point/New Pier/Maydon Wharf berths - Working normally for general cargo vessels. Maize terminal (Maydon Wharf 8) - 3 Vessels expected for June and 6 for July. Bunker supplies - Working normally, but could change daily due to bunching of vessels. Dry-dock/floating dock - 80 percent committed for June and 90 percent for July.

East London - General cargo/combi terminal/tanker berths - Busy but no delays expected at this stage. Dry-dock - Open for bookings. Copper 2,500 metric tonnes moving out per month. Tankers, 2 expected weekly. Port Elizabeth - Working normally, with 4 vessels in port. No delays expected on general, fruit or tanker berths. Ore berth - 1 Vessel berthed and a further 1 due 10/6, with berthing delay of approx. 20 hours experienced. Container berth - Still only 1 berth with 2 gantries. Hopefully back to 2 berths after 11/6. One vessels in port, 2 at anchorage and a further 2 due 10/6. Berthing delays of approx. 24 hrs. experienced at present but this should ease towards Thursday/Friday.

Cape Town - Breakbulk berths (general cargo) - Working normally, with vessels operating on arrival. Fruit berths - Fully occupied. Container terminal - Working normally, with vessels operating on arrival. Bunker berths - Numerous vessels by passing Cape Town due to non-availability of fuel oil. Dry-docks and repair quays fully occupied. Booking is essential. Saldanha Bay - Port working normally.

TUNISIA, June 8 - Sfax - Nine vessels in port operating of which 5 loading (4 fish, 1 bulk tsp). 3 Discharging (1 bulk maize, 2 general cargo). 1 Under arrest discharging bulk sulphur. Sousse - One vessel discharging vegetable oil. No delays. Tunis - Three vessels awaiting instructions, 1 discharging marble chips, 1 general cargo vessel. Rades - Three ro/ro vessels, 1 vessel discharging bananas. La Goulette - North side - 1 Vessel discharging pvc, 1 cereal vessel, 7 military vessels. South side - 1 Vessel discharging grain, 1 tanker discharging gasoil. Bizerte - June 10 - No berthing delays/congestion/strikes. One vessel discharging/loading fuel oil, 1 under arrest.

UNITED ARAB EMIRATES, June 1-7 - Dubai - No labour problems. 216 Vessels of which 93 containers, 11 general cargo, 7 general cargo/containers, 8 car carriers, 15 tankers, 1 livestock carrier, 1 passenger vessel, 12 naval vessels, 8 bunkering, under repairs, taking stores etc., 7 dhows, 13 barges, 15 tugs, 2 UAE naval vessels, 19 supply boats, 1 lpg tanker, 1 vlcc, 1 bulk oil, 1 chemical tanker. 5 Vessels loading at berth (3 containers, 2 general cargo). 11 Vessels under repair/laid-up (4 general cargo, 7 tankers). 51 Vessels due (28 containers, 15 general cargo, 8 tankers).

YEMEN, June 8 - Hodeidah - Eight vessels berthed of which 2 flour, 1 crude oil, 3 bulk wheat, 1 timber/steel, 1 containers. 4 Vessels anchored awaiting berths of which 2 bulk wheat, 1 flour, 1 government vessel. Berthing delays, containers 1 day, reefers 36 hours, general cargo (steel/timber/powder etc.) 2-3 days, bagged cargoes (sugar/rice/wheat flour etc.) 3-4 days, bulk wheat/corn 15-20 days. June 9 - Hodeidah - All berths occupied. 8 Vessels berthed of which 3 wheat, 2 flour, 1 containers, 1 vegetable oil, 1 timber. 4 Vessels anchored of which 2 wheat, 1 flour, 1 government cargo. Berthing delays, general cargo up to 2 days, bagged cargoes up to 4 days, bulk cargoes up to 6 days, containers up to 1 day. Mokha - All berths occupied, 1 vessel discharging wheat flour, 1 discharging cotton. No vessels anchored. Berthing delays of up to 2 days expected.
